rubric: PYTHON AS A FIRST LANGUAGE / EXCEPTIONS AND FILES / CHAPTER 16

slides.title: Files
slides.main: Files give a program memory: save, read, process data from outside.

items.title: Open
items.sub: Path and mode: r, w, a, x, b

slides.title: open and modes
slides.sub: Open a file, then close it
slides.main: For text, always give encoding; an open file must be closed.

body.text:
f = open("demo.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8")
f.write("hello\n")
f.close()
print(open("demo.txt", encoding="utf-8").read())

slides.title: The with statement
slides.main: With with, you can't forget to close.

body.text:
with open("demo.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write("hello\nworld\n")

with open("demo.txt", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    text = f.read()
print(text)
read() pulls the whole file into memory: for small files.

slides.title: Line-by-line reading
slides.sub: A file loops with for by itself
slides.main: One line in memory: reads files of any size.

body.text: Each line ends with \n; strip() usually removes it.

slides.title: Writing
slides.main: Only strings can be written: convert numbers with str.

body.text:
with open("log.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write("first")            # no \n: they stick together
    f.write("second\n")
    print("third", file=f)      # print adds \n itself

with open("log.txt", "a", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write(str(42) + "\n")

print(open("log.txt", encoding="utf-8").read())

slides.title: Encodings and bytes
slides.sub: Text in a file is bytes
slides.main: Binary mode uses bytes: images, archives, any non-text data.

body.text: UTF-8 opened as another encoding: UnicodeDecodeError or garbage.

slides.title: File position
slides.main: Read to the end: a second read() gives "", so rewind.

body.text:
with open("demo.txt", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    print(f.read(3))
    print(f.tell())
    f.seek(0)
    print(f.readline().strip())
    print(f.read().strip())

slides.title: How with works
slides.main: with guarantees cleanup: your own manager is a class with two methods.

slides.title: File errors
slides.main: try around open: open and catch beats checking first.

slides.title: Typical tasks
slides.sub: Open, loop over lines, closes itself
slides.main: Loops, strings, dicts, exceptions and files work as one mechanism.

slides.title: Temporary files
slides.main: Safe: no risk of overwriting others' files; ideal for tests.

body.text:
import os
import tempfile

with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as folder:
    path = os.path.join(folder, "data.txt")
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        f.write("temporary data")
    print(os.path.exists(path))
print(os.path.exists(path))

slides.title: Typical mistakes
slides.main: Two habits solve almost everything: with and explicit encoding.

body.text:
with open("demo.txt", "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    pass                      # wiped the file!

with open("demo.txt", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    print(repr(f.read()))
Also: relative path starts from launch folder; number instead of string in write; read() on a huge file.

slides.title: Summary
slides.main: with + encoding='utf-8': two habits for life.
